question: When can Vedic scripture override the word of Shiva?
premises: Vedic scripture does not override the word of Shiva merely because their domains differ.
A relation of subordination and overriding arises only when their domains are equal.
Such equality of domain may occur in some cases.
inference: Therefore, Vedic scripture can override the word of Shiva only in cases where both apply to the same domain.
uncertainties: The exact scope of viṣaya-tulyatva in this ritual-epistemic context is not fully specified in this verse.
plain_english: Thus, Vedic scripture does not override the word of Shiva simply because their domains differ. If, in some case, their domains are the same, then a relation of being overridden and overriding can arise.
